name: service-events
title: Events
description: Cookieless analytics and transactional server audit events built on OTLP, with inherited actor context, trusted geography and event-derived visits.
docs:
## Setup

Application events, audit classification and cookieless browser analytics use standard OTLP/HTTP JSON at `/api/otel/v1/logs`. No separate receiver or browser storage.

```ts
import { Layer, Redacted } from 'effect';
import { Events } from '@/services/events';
import { HttpApiOtlp } from '@/services/opentelemetry/api';

const events = Events.layer({
  origin: 'https://example.com',
  secret: Redacted.make(existingApplicationSecret),
}).pipe(Layer.provide(applicationSqlClientLayer));
const telemetry = HttpApiOtlp.layer.pipe(
  Layer.provide(Events.processorLayer.pipe(Layer.provide(events))),
);
```

| Configuration | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Service scope | Optional serviceName, then OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, then service.name in OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES; browser names cannot choose SQL scope |
| SQL injection | PostgreSQL/SQLite SqlClient enables persistence/migrations/visits; PgClient supplies generic SqlClient too |
| No SQL | Browser enrichment/forwarding only; no migrations/session IDs; server track fails explicitly |
| Layer composition | Provide SQL to Events before acquisition, not as a sibling; baseLayer leaves migrations to the application |
| origin | Browser Origin allowlist, not authentication |
| secret | Stable server secret of 32+ characters, shared across instances; never sent to browser |
| geolocation omitted | No IP/geography lookup and no automatic visitor/session attribution |
| geolocation: 'cloudflare' | Validated Cloudflare IP/country/region/city headers; requires verified ingress with origin-bypass protection |
| geolocation(request) | Custom Effect returning optional ip/country/region/city fields or null; no Cloudflare fallback |
| Request auth | Verified user.id/organization.id log annotations supply browser identity; invalid annotations return 503 before writes |
| identity(request) | Optional fallback for other auth integrations, returning verified userId/organizationId or null; request auth annotations take precedence as a whole |

Custom geolocation returns numeric IPv4/IPv6 ip, uppercase two-letter country, uppercase subdivision suffix region (ON becomes CA-ON with country CA), and/or a nonempty city up to 128 characters. Return only ip for visitors/visits without geography, only geography to omit visitor IDs, or null for none. IP is used only for daily hashing, never stored automatically. Browser lookup runs once per validated batch; server lookup runs per request-scoped track call, never for background events. Provider failures/invalid results fail browser ingestion with 503 or server recording without silently falling back.

Browser identity claims are discarded. Without request auth annotations or a fallback identity, events are anonymous. With KrakStack Auth, provide `AuthMiddleware.routerLayer({ paths: ['/api/otel/v1/logs'] })` to the telemetry route layer. AuthMiddleware supplies verified attribution using its session lookup; no custom Events identity callback is needed. Auth failures return errors rather than silently becoming anonymous. This authenticates attribution only: ActorRequired still owns project authorization and CurrentActor. Use distinct service names for environments sharing storage. Unsupported SQL dialects fail acquisition. SQL failure never silently disables persistence.

## Server API

```ts
const program = Effect.gen(function* () {
  const events = yield* Events;
  const sql = yield* SqlClient.SqlClient;
  yield* Effect.gen(function* () {
    // Apply the authorized business change here.
    yield* events.track({
      eventId: `document:${requestId}:deleted`,
      name: 'document.deleted',
      category: 'audit',
      properties: { document_id: documentId },
    });
  }).pipe(sql.withTransaction);
});
```

| Contract | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Input | eventId, name; optional category, properties, identity, timestamp |
| Category | analytics by default; audit requires server app.actor.type/id annotations |
| Domain details | Target/outcome are ordinary properties validated by caller-owned Effect schemas; no inferred success or mandatory generic target |
| Storage | Requires SqlClient, joins the same SqlClient transaction, returns `{ eventId, inserted }` |
| Request context | An available HttpServerRequest enables the same visitor/session and geo/device resolution as browser ingestion |
| Explicit context | Trusted server annotations override derived context; untrusted session headers and event properties do not select a session |
| Background events | No automatic visitor/session without a request or trusted IP/User-Agent; explicit annotations still work |
| Deduplication | Primary key (service_name, source, event_id); trusted browser/server source is assigned by the recording path, never client attributes |
| Identical retry | Returns inserted:false and retains the authoritative stored record |
| Conflicting ID | Different caller-owned content fails with EventConflictError; browser batches return 409 and roll back |
| Delivery | Local OTLP JSON only; optionally emit ServerOtlp.event after commit |

Page views and request-scoped server searches/views share visits when the trusted service, secret, provider IP and User-Agent match. Both paths extend activity under the same transaction and visitor lock; IDs are stored in SQL and OTLP. No continuation tokens or browser state are introduced. Backend-to-backend requests identify the calling backend, not individual end users; separate journeys require application-validated context. Browser DNT/GPC does not disable explicit server track calls; apply application-owned opt-out policy before recording.

There is one track method. Audit is a policy classification, not different durability or immutable storage. Auth owns actor verification/API-key ownership; MCP/AI layers own their context. Server log annotations are inherited, so only annotate safe-to-persist data. Annotated identity replaces explicit identity as a whole; explicit category wins over annotations/properties. app.actor.* and app.event.* are custom conventions, not OTel audit standards. Failed/denied attempts need a transaction that commits.

## Browser

```ts
import { BrowserEvents } from '@/services/events/browser';
BrowserEvents.layer({ serviceName: 'my-app-web', locale: () => 'en' });
```

Use one BrowserEvents layer instead of a second BrowserOtlp layer. Enable OTLP logs export.

| API / option | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| track(name, properties?, options?) | Properties become app.*; returns an Effect |
| page(options?) | Page view with name/category/path/properties |
| pageViews:false | Manual integration; automatic initial/SPA pathname views otherwise enabled |
| enabled:false | Disable application events and passed-through Web Vitals |
| Privacy | DNT/GPC respected; no cookies or browser identity state |
| sanitizePath | Replace personal path identifiers with route templates |
| webVitals:true | Independent BrowserOtlp collection, not SQL storage |
| Trust | Always analytics; client actor/audit/executor claims discarded |

Web Vitals follow OTel browser conventions independently of Events/SQL: browser.web_vital, standard browser.web_vital.* attributes, lowercase names, double values/deltas, no automatic page/identity context or DOM attribution.

## Storage and visits

One events data table, plus the existing events_migrations runner metadata. PostgreSQL uses JSONB and GIN jsonb_path_ops; SQLite uses JSON text. Rows hold source, event name/type, occurrence/receipt times, user/organization/visitor IDs, optional session_id and per-event payload_json. Category/actor/business properties are OTLP attributes. No session metadata table, outbox, worker or cleanup API.

| Visit rule | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Lookup | Latest browser or server event for service/anonymous visitor |
| Under 30 minutes of receipt inactivity | Reuse session.id; otherwise new UUID |
| Retry | Reuse original record/session/receipt time, including across midnight or changed/missing request metadata |
| Concurrency | Transactional lookup/insert; PostgreSQL advisory lock or SQLite writer lock before reads |
| Timeline | Filter session_id; order occurred_at/event_id |
| Midnight UTC | Daily visitor rotation splits new visits, not retries |
| Missing provider IP/UA | No automatic visitor/session for new events; retries preserve original attribution |

Retain at least 30 minutes for active visits. Daily IDs are approximate service/day HMACs of trusted IP+UA. Geolocation is optional: choose Cloudflare behind verified ingress or supply an application-owned provider. Server UA parsing supplies browser/OS/device; missing UA gives unknown context. Referrer hostname and UTM fields are included, not a full attribution engine. No dashboards/funnels/retention UI.

Scope queries by service and authorized organization/user, derived from verified access, never unchecked input. Session IDs are grouping keys, not access tokens. Own category-aware retention, permissions and backups. No immutability/compliance guarantee, content hashing or immutable archive.

Committed browser application batches succeed despite best-effort collector failure (five-second timeout); mixed batches preserve generic delivery semantics. No guaranteed central delivery.

| Boundary | Policy |
| --- | --- |
| Scope | krakstack.application.events; app.event.schema.version=1; generic krakstack.events remains separate |
| Browser context | analytics.* retained; producer resource preserved |
| Request | JSON; 64 KiB; at most 100 application records; matching Origin |
| Timestamp | Previous hour through one minute ahead |
| Privacy | No automatic raw IP/UA, full URLs, titles or ad IDs; properties caller-owned |

Install service-events or @krak-stack/registry/events, /events/browser, /events/migrations. The unreleased initial schema includes source; explicitly migrate/export experimental local databases before switching. Apply edge rate limits/bot filtering and keep IDs out of metric/Loki labels.
